The `toolbox` binary is the operator and user surface. Catalog **reads** are the same over the CLI, MCP, and HTTP: one authorization path, one snapshot model.

This page is **generated from the CLI** (`toolbox describe` plus each command’s `--help`). Do not edit it by hand — run `python3 scripts/generate-cli-docs.py` (or `npm run generate:cli-docs` from `site/`). Use `--check` in CI to fail when the committed page is stale.

Install: [Quickstart](/toolbox/start/quickstart/) or [Install a release](/toolbox/start/install/).

## Commands

| Command | About | MCP tool |
|---|---|---|
| [`toolbox actions`](#actions) | Actions available on an entity | `list_actions` |
| [`toolbox assess brief`](#assess-brief) | What to judge an entity on: the rubric's criteria, the entity's facts, its subject hash, and a template and file path for the assessment | — |
| [`toolbox assess check`](#assess-check) | Validate the portal's assessments/ files and list, per rubric, which entities are assessed (fresh), assessed against an older version (stale), or not assessed (missing) | — |
| [`toolbox assess submit`](#assess-submit) | Validate assessment files and push them to a running server as `assessment` records of a remote connector (for portals whose assessments live in Postgres, not in a repository) | — |
| [`toolbox campaign`](#campaign) | One campaign's progress over existing scorecards (entities still missing the goal). Without a name, lists the campaigns | `campaign_report` |
| [`toolbox connector drive`](#connector-drive) | Drive a connector binary over stdio: one `resync` of the named kinds, print each `record` as NDJSON (`kind`, `externalId`, `data`). No portal required — for local dumps while authoring. Pass config with --config (JSON) or rely on TOOLBOX_CONNECTOR_CONFIG in the environment. Use `--format catalog` to emit harness-shaped `{kind,id,data}` lines (catalog `id` = `externalId` with a leading `{kind}:` stripped) and `--out` to write a file | — |
| [`toolbox connector records`](#connector-records) | Run one resync of a portal's connector and print its records (NDJSON): what a tool reported before any rule reads it. Lint records carry `command`, which reproduces their findings with the tool alone | — |
| [`toolbox connector test`](#connector-test) | Run the conformance kit against a connector binary in in-image (stdio) mode. Its config comes from the portal manifest (with --config overriding it as JSON) | — |
| [`toolbox derive`](#derive) | Recompute derived state from fixtures and print a summary, or write the reference-format files (expected/*.json, authz/tuples.expected.json) to --out | — |
| [`toolbox describe portal`](#describe-portal) | Every part of portals as records — `kind`, `field`, `connector`, `scorecard`, `rule`: manifest facts, content hashes, usage, CEL size and loops, test coverage, outcomes over fixtures and (with --results) on real data | — |
| [`toolbox doctor`](#doctor) | Check that every in-image connector resolves and every declared tool is at its pinned version; exit 1 when something is missing | — |
| [`toolbox explain`](#explain) | Why a field has its value (--field) or why a rule passes or fails (--rule scorecard/rule) | `explain` |
| [`toolbox get`](#get) | Read one entity (fields and where each came from) | `get` |
| [`toolbox graph`](#graph) | Neighbours of an entity | `graph` |
| [`toolbox install`](#install) | Download the portal's released executable connectors (`github:owner/repo[/app]@version`) for this platform, verify them against toolbox.lock (pinning them the first time), and unpack them into the cache | — |
| [`toolbox mcp`](#mcp) | A stdio MCP server bridging to the portal's /mcp endpoint | — |
| [`toolbox owner`](#owner) | Who owns an entity and why (CODEOWNERS evidence) | `owner_of` |
| [`toolbox plan`](#plan) | Show what a manifest change would do: two recomputes over the same inputs, then a diff | — |
| [`toolbox push`](#push) | Send a portal's fixtures to a running server through the ingest API (one batch per connector, then native values), and wait for the snapshot that contains them | — |
| [`toolbox query`](#query) | Entities of a kind matching a CEL filter over `entity` (and `scores`) | `query` |
| [`toolbox refresh`](#refresh) | Ask the connectors behind an entity to re-read it, and wait for the fresh snapshot | `refresh_entity` |
| [`toolbox report`](#report) | Score a repository locally: run the portal's in-image connectors once (or use its fixtures), recompute, and print every scorecard with the evidence for failing rules. With --baseline, compare against a committed results file (a ratchet): regressions exit 1, --update records improvements, --ci also fails when the file is out of date | — |
| [`toolbox score`](#score) | Scorecard levels and rule outcomes for one entity | `scorecard_status` |
| [`toolbox scorecard`](#scorecard) | One scorecard across every entity: level counts, failing rules and evidence (a work list). Without a name, lists the scorecards | `scorecard_report` |
| [`toolbox search`](#search) | Find entities by name or title | `search` |
| [`toolbox serve`](#serve) | Run the server: snapshot loop + REST API. Uses Postgres when --database-url (or DATABASE_URL) is set, otherwise an in-memory store (optionally preloaded with fixtures) | — |
| [`toolbox test`](#test) | Recompute derived state from the portal's fixtures and run its expectation files (tests/*.test.yaml). Exit code 1 if any expectation fails | — |
| [`toolbox token create`](#token-create) | Create a token for a user (the subject: a login or an email) and print it once | — |
| [`toolbox tools config`](#tools-config) | Print an installer's input from the portal's pins: a mise `[tools]` table, an aqua.yaml package list, or PyPI requirements (for uv, pipx or pip) | — |
| [`toolbox tools find`](#tools-find) | List the tools a repository already uses (config files, CI and hook commands, package manifests), whether each is in the portal's box, and the slot that would carry it. Evidence for an agent to check (skill find-tools), not a verdict | — |
| [`toolbox tools install`](#tools-install) | Install every tool the portal pins that isn't already on the PATH at its version, by running an installer: mise, uv, pipx or pip (auto: the first available that the tool declares an id for). Then run `toolbox doctor` | — |
| [`toolbox validate`](#validate) | Validate a portal: manifest schema, cross-references, action input forms, CEL, files and fixtures. Exit code 0 when valid, 1 when there are errors, 2 when it can't be loaded | — |
| [`toolbox vendor`](#vendor) | Copy a package into the portal (`<portal>/packages/<name>`, without its tests) so the portal needs no network: from a directory, or a `github:` package `toolbox install` cached | — |

## Command help

Help text below is taken verbatim from `toolbox <command> --help`.

### `actions`

```text
Actions available on an entity

Usage: toolbox actions [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>  Entity id

Options:
      --url <URL>        Portal URL [env: TOOLBOX_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:8080]
      --token <TOKEN>    Personal access token [env: TOOLBOX_TOKEN=]
      --as <AS_USER>     Dev servers only: act as this user [env: TOOLBOX_AS=]
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>  Output: md (default), json or yaml [default: md]
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### `assess brief`

```text
What to judge an entity on: the rubric's criteria, the entity's facts, its subject hash, and a template and file path for the assessment

Usage: toolbox assess brief [OPTIONS] <ENTITY>

Arguments:
  <ENTITY>  Entity id, e.g. rule:portal/user-mcp/contract-tested

Options:
      --rubric <RUBRIC>  Rubric name (default: the only rubric for the entity's kind)
      --portal <PORTAL>  A portal directory (containing toolbox.yaml) or a manifest file [default: .]
      --fixtures         Use the portal's fixtures instead of running its connectors
      --skip <SKIP>      Connectors not to run (comma-separated), e.g. a slow runner
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>  Output: md (instructions for an agent, default) or json [default: md]
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### `assess check`

```text
Validate the portal's assessments/ files and list, per rubric, which entities are assessed (fresh), assessed against an older version (stale), or not assessed (missing)

Usage: toolbox assess check [OPTIONS] [PORTAL]

Arguments:
  [PORTAL]  A portal directory (containing toolbox.yaml) or a manifest file [default: .]

Options:
      --fixtures         Use the portal's fixtures instead of running its connectors
      --skip <SKIP>      Connectors not to run (comma-separated), e.g. a slow runner
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>  Output: md (default) or json [default: md]
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### `assess submit`

```text
Validate assessment files and push them to a running server as `assessment` records of a remote connector (for portals whose assessments live in Postgres, not in a repository)

Usage: toolbox assess submit [OPTIONS] <FILES>...

Arguments:
  <FILES>...  Assessment files (YAML or JSON)

Options:
      --portal <PORTAL>        The portal whose rubrics the files must match [default: .]
      --url <URL>              The running server [env: TOOLBOX_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:8080]
      --connector <CONNECTOR>  The remote connector the records belong to (dev servers, without a token) [default: assessments]
      --token <TOKEN>          That connector's token [env: TOOLBOX_CONNECTOR_TOKEN=]
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

### `campaign`

```text
One campaign's progress over existing scorecards (entities still missing the goal). Without a name, lists the campaigns

Usage: toolbox campaign [OPTIONS] [NAME]

Arguments:
  [NAME]  Campaign name

Options:
      --portal <PORTAL>      Run this portal locally instead of asking a server (a repo portal: no server needed)
      --baseline <BASELINE>  With --portal: the baseline whose recorded campaign starts the paydown is counted from
      --skip <SKIP>          With --portal: connectors not to run (comma-separated)
      --url <URL>            Portal URL [env: TOOLBOX_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:8080]
      --token <TOKEN>        Personal access token [env: TOOLBOX_TOKEN=]
      --as <AS_USER>         Dev servers only: act as this user [env: TOOLBOX_AS=]
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>      Output: md (default), json or yaml [default: md]
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

### `connector drive`

```text
Drive a connector binary over stdio: one `resync` of the named kinds, print each `record` as NDJSON (`kind`, `externalId`, `data`). No portal required — for local dumps while authoring. Pass config with --config (JSON) or rely on TOOLBOX_CONNECTOR_CONFIG in the environment. Use `--format catalog` to emit harness-shaped `{kind,id,data}` lines (catalog `id` = `externalId` with a leading `{kind}:` stripped) and `--out` to write a file

Usage: toolbox connector drive [OPTIONS] -- <PROGRAM>...

Arguments:
  <PROGRAM>...  The connector program and its arguments

Options:
      --kinds <KINDS>    Record kinds to resync (comma-separated), e.g. project,issue
      --config <CONFIG>  JSON object set as TOOLBOX_CONNECTOR_CONFIG for the child
      --format <FORMAT>  Output shape: `records` (default) or `catalog` (`kind`/`id`/`data`, sorted) [default: records] [possible values: records, catalog]
      --out <OUT>        Write NDJSON to this path instead of stdout (parent dirs must exist)
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### `connector records`

```text
Run one resync of a portal's connector and print its records (NDJSON): what a tool reported before any rule reads it. Lint records carry `command`, which reproduces their findings with the tool alone

Usage: toolbox connector records [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>

Options:
      --name <NAME>      The connector's name in the manifest
      --portal <PORTAL>  Portal directory or manifest [default: .]
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### `connector test`

```text
Run the conformance kit against a connector binary in in-image (stdio) mode. Its config comes from the portal manifest (with --config overriding it as JSON)

Usage: toolbox connector test [OPTIONS] --name <NAME> -- <PROGRAM>...

Arguments:
  <PROGRAM>...  The connector program and its arguments

Options:
      --name <NAME>      The connector's name in the manifest
      --portal <PORTAL>  Portal directory or manifest [default: .]
      --config <CONFIG>  JSON merged over the manifest's connector config (e.g. an apiUrl for a mock)
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### `derive`

```text
Recompute derived state from fixtures and print a summary, or write the reference-format files (expected/*.json, authz/tuples.expected.json) to --out

Arguments:
  [PATH]  A portal directory (containing toolbox.yaml) or a manifest file [default: .]

Options:
```

```text
Every part of portals as records — `kind`, `field`, `connector`, `scorecard`, `rule`: manifest facts, content hashes, usage, CEL size and loops, test coverage, outcomes over fixtures and (with --results) on real data

Options:
```


```text

Arguments:
```

```text
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### `report`

```text
Score a repository locally: run the portal's in-image connectors once (or use its fixtures), recompute, and print every scorecard with the evidence for failing rules. With --baseline, compare against a committed results file (a ratchet): regressions exit 1, --update records improvements, --ci also fails when the file is out of date

Usage: toolbox report [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]  A portal directory (containing toolbox.yaml) or a manifest file [default: .]

Options:
      --fixtures             Use the portal's fixtures instead of running its connectors
      --skip <SKIP>          Connectors not to run (comma-separated), e.g. a slow runner
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>      Output: md (default), json (scores, ratchet results and campaigns), failures (a JSON list of every failing rule: scorecard, rule, entity, path, the entity's scalar fields, measure, evidence, fix), html (one self-contained page), or web (a directory: the `<toolbox-report>` element, its JSON, and that page). A host fills the element's header, nav, and footer slots; pass --out DIR for web [default: md]
      --out <OUT>            Write the output to this file instead of stdout
      --html <HTML>          Also write the one-page HTML report to this file (from the same run)
      --baseline <BASELINE>  Results file to compare against (the ratchet)
      --update               With --baseline: write the new results when nothing regressed (creates a missing file)
      --ci                   With --baseline: fail when the results differ from the file in any way
      --fail-on-unknown      With --baseline: fail (exit 1) when a rule's outcome is unknown although its connector ran (not excused by --skip), such as a kit whose `optional: true` tool isn't installed. A plain check passes then, so a gate that must not run without its tools should pass this
      --accept <ACCEPT>      With --update: record regressions in these scorecards (comma-separated) instead of failing, for an intended change to a standard (a tighter threshold, a new pattern). They are listed; regressions in other scorecards still fail
      --keep-campaigns       With --accept: keep each campaign's recorded start, so the accepted findings show as the campaign going backwards (a tool upgrade or a new tool that reports more). Without it, --accept restarts the campaigns over those scorecards (a changed standard)
      --verdict <VERDICT>    Write the ratchet's verdict as JSON to this file (result, exit code, regressions, improvements), for any CI system to read
      --all                  Markdown: list every entity, not only those with a failing or unknown rule
      --against <AGAINST>    Compare with the portal's results at this git commit (e.g. HEAD~1, or a pull request's base), scored in a temporary worktree, instead of with a baseline file: what this change made worse or better. Exit 1 on a regression; nothing is written
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

### `serve`

```text
Run the server: snapshot loop + REST API. Uses Postgres when --database-url (or DATABASE_URL) is set, otherwise an in-memory store (optionally preloaded with fixtures)

Usage: toolbox serve [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]  A portal directory (containing toolbox.yaml) or a manifest file [default: .]

Options:
      --listen <LISTEN>              Address to listen on. `TOOLBOX_LISTEN` and `--listen` win. Otherwise, when `PORT` is set, the server binds `0.0.0.0:$PORT` (the Cloud Run contract). With neither, it binds `127.0.0.1:8080` [env: TOOLBOX_LISTEN=]
      --database-url <DATABASE_URL>  Postgres URL; without it the store is in memory and lost on exit [env: DATABASE_URL=]
      --fixtures                     In-memory mode only: load the portal's fixtures at start
  -h, --help                         Print help
```

```text
Usage: toolbox test [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]  A portal directory (containing toolbox.yaml) or a manifest file [default: .]

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>  Output format [default: text] [possible values: text, json]
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### `token create`

```text

Usage: toolbox token create [OPTIONS] --user <USER> --database-url <DATABASE_URL>

Options:
      --user <USER>                  The token's subject: a login or an email
      --label <LABEL>                A note to recognise the token by
      --database-url <DATABASE_URL>  The portal's Postgres, where token hashes are stored [env: DATABASE_URL=]
  -h, --help                         Print help
```

### `tools config`

```text
Print an installer's input from the portal's pins: a mise `[tools]` table, an aqua.yaml package list, or PyPI requirements (for uv, pipx or pip)

Usage: toolbox tools config --for <INSTALLER> [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]  A portal directory (containing toolbox.yaml) or a manifest file [default: .]

Options:
      --for <INSTALLER>  mise, aqua or pypi
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### `tools find`

```text
List the tools a repository already uses (config files, CI and hook commands, package manifests), whether each is in the portal's box, and the slot that would carry it. Evidence for an agent to check (skill find-tools), not a verdict

Usage: toolbox tools find [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]  The repository root [default: .]

Options:
      --portal <PORTAL>  The portal to compare with (default: the root's toolbox.yaml, else portal/toolbox.yaml)
      --format <FORMAT>  Output format [default: text] [possible values: text, json]
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### `tools install`

```text
Install every tool the portal pins that isn't already on the PATH at its version, by running an installer: mise, uv, pipx or pip (auto: the first available that the tool declares an id for). Then run `toolbox doctor`

Usage: toolbox tools install [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]  A portal directory (containing toolbox.yaml) or a manifest file [default: .]

Options:
      --via <VIA>  The installer: auto, mise, uv, pipx or pip (aqua installs from `tools config --for aqua`) [default: auto]
      --dry-run    Print the install commands without running them
  -h, --help       Print help
```

### `validate`

```text
Validate a portal: manifest schema, cross-references, action input forms, CEL, files and fixtures. Exit code 0 when valid, 1 when there are errors, 2 when it can't be loaded

Usage: toolbox validate [OPTIONS] [PATH]

Arguments:
  [PATH]  A portal directory (containing toolbox.yaml) or a manifest file [default: .]

Options:
      --format <FORMAT>  Output format [default: text] [possible values: text, json]
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### `vendor`

```text
Copy a package into the portal (`<portal>/packages/<name>`, without its tests) so the portal needs no network: from a directory, or a `github:` package `toolbox install` cached

Usage: toolbox vendor [OPTIONS] <SPEC>

Arguments:
  <SPEC>  A package directory, or `github:owner/repo[/subdir]@version`

Options:
      --portal <PORTAL>  The portal to vendor it into (a directory containing toolbox.yaml) [default: .]
  -h, --help             Print help
```
